title: Adi Dravidar Welfare TN: Scholarships and Schemes
meta_description: Adi Dravidar Welfare Department Tamil Nadu runs scholarships and hostels for SC/ST students. Income Rs 2.5 lakh limit. All benefits at tnadw.tn.gov.in.

hero.one_liner: Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department TN runs scholarships, hostels, and incentives for SC and ST students from Class 1 to PhD. Income limit Rs 2.5 lakh.

what_is_it: The Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department is one of Tamil Nadu's oldest dedicated welfare departments, running educational scholarships, government hostels, and financial assistance schemes for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe communities across every level of education from primary school to postgraduate study. It is not just a scholarship-issuing body but operates its own schools, hostel networks, and targeted incentive programmes designed to reduce dropout rates at every transition point in a student's academic journey.

The department serves students from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Minority Muslims, and Converted Christians in Tamil Nadu, and the official portal for all department information is tnadw.tn.gov.in. Scholarship applications for most programmes under this department are submitted through the Tamil Nadu State Scholarship Portal at ssp.tn.gov.in.

how_to_apply.title: Verify Your Eligibility
how_to_apply.description: Confirm that you belong to a Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Minority Muslim, or Converted Christian community as defined by Tamil Nadu government records, and that your annual family income from all sources does not exceed Rs 2,50,000 for most scholarship categories or Rs 1,00,000 for Class 11-12 scholarships. You must be enrolled in a recognised educational institution in Tamil Nadu and must have been a permanent resident of the state for more than five years, and male students applying for hostel seats additionally need to confirm they live more than 5 kilometres from their institution.

how_to_apply.title: Collect Required Documents
how_to_apply.description: You will need a community certificate issued by the Revenue Department confirming your SC or ST or Minority category, an income certificate from the Tehsildar or Revenue Divisional Officer reflecting the current financial year, your Aadhaar card, recent academic marksheets, a current enrollment or bonafide certificate from your institution, and your bank account passbook showing the account number and IFSC code. For the GoI Post-Matric Scholarship, you will also need a fee receipt from your institution showing the compulsory fees paid, since this scheme reimburses actual compulsory fees rather than a fixed amount.

how_to_apply.title: Register on the Tamil Nadu State Scholarship Portal
how_to_apply.description: Go to ssp.tn.gov.in and click student registration to create an account using your Aadhaar number and the mobile number linked to your Aadhaar. After registering and logging in, the portal displays scholarship schemes for which you may be eligible based on your community, course level, and income details, and you can apply for the state ADW scholarship and the GoI Post-Matric Scholarship independently through separate applications on the same portal.

how_to_apply.title: Fill and Submit the Online Application
how_to_apply.description: Complete the application form with accurate details about your community, family income, institution, course, and bank account, and upload scanned copies of all required documents in the formats specified on the portal. Errors in community certificate details or income figures are the most common reasons for rejection, so review every field against your original documents before submitting, and save the application number and a downloaded copy of the submitted form after completion.

how_to_apply.title: Institution Head Submits Physical Hard Copies
how_to_apply.description: After your online submission, your school principal or college head must verify your enrollment on the portal and also compile physical copies of your application and supporting documents and dispatch them by post to the district Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare office. The online submission alone is not sufficient for processing, and many applications stall because this physical dispatch step is not completed by the institution, so confirm in person with your administrative office that the hard copies have been sent.

how_to_apply.title: District ADW Office Verifies Your Application
how_to_apply.description: District ADW officials review the received applications and cross-check community certificates and income documents with revenue department records, and applications with inconsistencies may be returned for correction before the verification deadline. Once verified, the district office forwards approved applications to the Directorate of Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare in Chennai for final sanction, and maintaining exact name consistency across your caste certificate, Aadhaar, and income certificate is the most important factor in smooth verification.

how_to_apply.title: Payment Credited Directly to Your Bank Account
how_to_apply.description: Once the directorate sanctions your scholarship, the amount is credited directly to your bank account through ECS, with no cash payment and no cheque issued at any stage. Your bank account must be active, Aadhaar-linked, and in your own name, since Aadhaar seeding is mandatory for ECS to work and failed seeding is the most common technical reason for non-receipt even after sanction. Scholarship renewal for subsequent years requires a fresh application within the announced window, fresh income and enrollment documents, and a fresh physical submission from your institution each year.

extra_sections.heading: What Is the Adi Dravidar Welfare Department
content: Tamil Nadu operates a 69 percent reservation structure for socially backward communities, one of the highest in India, and the Adi Dravidar Welfare Department directly administers the educational support infrastructure for SC communities within this framework. The department's role extends well beyond reservations in admissions to include financial support that makes attendance and completion of education economically feasible for students who would otherwise drop out.

The department runs its own network of government schools across Tamil Nadu, known as Adi Dravidar Welfare schools, and students in these schools receive free textbooks, uniforms, guides, and question banks as part of their enrollment. This support is provided in addition to eligibility for the scholarship amounts available to all SC students across recognised institutions in the state.

extra_sections.heading: Adi Dravidar Welfare TN: Key Numbers
Who the Department Serves
content: At the primary and middle school level, the department focuses on keeping girl students enrolled through annual cash incentives at specific class thresholds. These incentives are designed to signal value to families and offset the small recurring costs that often lead to girls being withdrawn from school before they reach the secondary level.

extra_sections.title: The Income Limits, Explained
extra_sections.content:
For most scholarships the annual family income limit is Rs 2.5 lakh. For Class 11 and 12 scholarships the limit is stricter at Rs 1 lakh.

Income is verified through a certificate from the Tehsildar or Revenue Divisional Officer. The combined income of all family sources is counted.

extra_sections.heading: The Scholarship Income Rules
content: At the college level, the department runs two parallel scholarship tracks simultaneously: a state-funded academic expense scholarship and the Government of India Post-Matric Scholarship scheme for SC students. The state scheme covers annual academic expenses while the central scheme covers compulsory fees and provides a monthly maintenance allowance.

All scholarship payments under this department are transferred directly to the student's bank account through the Electronic Clearing Service system, with no cash disbursement and no intermediary involved. Students need a bank account in their own name with Aadhaar seeding active before applying, since failed Aadhaar-ECS linking is the most common technical cause of payment delay even after a scholarship is approved.

extra_sections.heading: SC Adi Dravidar Scholarship Amounts by Education Level
School and College Scholarships
content: Students enrolled in Adi Dravidar Welfare schools and government schools receive free textbooks from Class 1 to Class 12, and students in Classes 9 to 12 additionally get free guides and question bank books to support Board exam preparation. All students in ADW schools and hostels also receive four sets of free school uniforms every year at no cost.

extra_sections.heading: Hostels for SC and ST Students
content: The Adi Dravidar Welfare Department runs government hostels across Tamil Nadu for SC and ST school students, college students, and ITI trainees, providing free accommodation and basic facilities for students who study far from their homes. Male students must live more than 5 kilometres from their institution to be eligible, while girl students face no distance restriction and may apply regardless of proximity.

Hostel applications are made through the district ADW office, with seats allocated based on availability and preference given to students from economically weaker families. Students residing in ADW hostels are also covered by the department's general welfare provisions including free textbooks and uniforms.

extra_sections.title: Startup Grant for Law Graduates
extra_sections.desc:
SC and ST law graduates who set up independent legal practice get a Rs 50,000 startup grant.

This is one of the department's many benefits that reach beyond school into professional life, alongside tools and appliance assistance for BPL families.

extra_sections.heading: Beyond School: Law Grads and Tools
content: The department also provides a startup grant of Rs 50,000 to SC and ST law graduates who set up independent legal practice after completing their degree. This one-time grant addresses the specific barrier of chamber setup costs, registration fees, and initial operating expenses that prevent many first-generation lawyers from marginalised communities from establishing themselves independently after law school.

The tool and appliance assistance scheme under the ADW department extends support beyond education to SC and ST individuals below the poverty line who need tools or equipment to run their livelihood. This scheme operates as a parallel track to the educational scholarships under the same department umbrella and does not require the applicant to be a student.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply for the Scholarship

steps.title: Confirm eligibility
steps.desc: Confirm your community, that family income is within Rs 2.5 lakh (Rs 1 lakh for Class 11-12), and that you study in a recognised institution.

steps.title: Gather documents
steps.desc: Community certificate, income certificate from the Tehsildar or RDO, Aadhaar, bank passbook, and your previous marksheet.

steps.title: Apply online
steps.desc: Register on the scholarship portal, fill the form, choose the correct scheme (state ADW or GoI Post-Matric), and submit.

steps.desc: Your school or college head dispatches the physical documents. After verification, payment is credited by ECS to your bank account.

items.title: Pre-Matric (Class 9-10)
items.sub: Rs 2,250 a year for day scholars and Rs 4,500 for hostellers, covering academic expenses.

items.title: Post-Matric (Class 11 onwards)
items.sub: Two parallel tracks: a state academic-expense scholarship and the Government of India Post-Matric Scholarship.

items.title: Girl-student incentives
items.sub: Annual cash incentives from Class 3 onwards, starting at Rs 500 a year, to keep girls enrolled.

items.title: Higher education special
items.sub: Rs 7,500 a year for degree and polytechnic, Rs 8,000 a year for post-graduate and professional courses for hostellers.

extra_sections.heading: Free Materials and Special Admission
content: The special school admission scheme for Class 11 and 12 selects the 10 highest-performing SC and ST students per district based on their Class 10 Board exam scores and arranges their admission to distinguished private schools. This programme gives academically exceptional students access to better-resourced environments for their final two school years, improving their preparation for competitive college admissions.

For students from families engaged in occupations historically classified as unclean, such as manual scavenging or sanitation work, the department provides dedicated pre-matric scholarship support for children enrolled in Class 1 to 10 regardless of the standard income eligibility conditions. These students are also prioritised for hostel seat allocation at the district level.

items.title: Government hostels
items.sub: For SC and ST school, college, and ITI students, with seats allocated by the district ADW office, priority to those far from home.

items.title: Free textbooks and uniforms
items.sub: Free textbooks from Class 1 to 12 in ADW and government schools, plus uniform sets and Board exam guides.

items.title: Special school admission
items.sub: The top 10 SC and ST Class 10 scorers per district get admission to distinguished private schools for Class 11 and 12.

items.title: Unclean-occupation families
items.sub: Children of families in manual scavenging or sanitation get pre-matric scholarship regardless of income or community.

extra_sections.heading: The Chief Minister's Award and Merit
content: The Chief Minister's Award is a merit recognition component within the department's programmes, given to the 1,000 highest-scoring SC and ST boys and 1,000 highest-scoring SC and ST girls in the Tamil Nadu Higher Secondary Certificate Board exams each year. Each awardee receives Rs 3,000 per year for five years, a sustained incentive to encourage high academic performers to pursue university education rather than entering the workforce at the HSC stage.

From each district, the department selects the 10 highest-ranking SC and ST students in the Class 10 Board exam and arranges their admission to distinguished private schools for Class 11 and 12. This bridge programme gives exceptional students access to better-resourced academic environments for their final school years, improving their chances at competitive college admissions.

extra_sections.title: The Chief Minister's Award
extra_sections.content:
The Chief Minister's Award goes to the 1,000 highest-scoring SC and ST students in the Board exams. Each gets Rs 3,000 a year for five years.

From each district, the 10 highest-ranking SC and ST Class 10 students are also selected for special school admission in top institutions.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply and Submit Documents
content: Students who submit the online application but whose school or college head does not dispatch the physical hard copies to the district ADW office often find their applications stalled indefinitely in the system. The online submission is necessary but not sufficient for processing, so visit your institution's administrative office after submitting and confirm in person that the physical documents have been sent to the district office.

To check scholarship status after applying, log into ssp.tn.gov.in and navigate to the application status section, which shows your application's stage from submission through district verification to final sanction. For applications pending more than eight weeks after physical documents were dispatched, visiting the district ADW office in person with your application number resolves most cases faster than portal follow-ups or helpline calls.

extra_sections.heading: Common Problems and How to Avoid Them

items.title: Missing the deadline
items.sub: The single most common reason students lose a full year of scholarship. Note the application window and apply early.

items.title: Name mismatch
items.sub: A difference between your community certificate name and Aadhaar name triggers rejection. Make them consistent first.

items.title: Outdated income certificate
items.sub: Tamil Nadu requires a current-year income certificate. An old one is rejected at verification.

items.title: Hard copies not dispatched
items.sub: Online submission is not enough. Your school or college must dispatch physical documents to the district office.

extra_sections.heading: Renewal and Choosing the Right Scheme
content: Scholarship renewal for subsequent academic years is not automatic, and many students who received a scholarship in their first year of college incorrectly assume it continues without action. Each year, students must reapply through the portal within the announced window, attach fresh income and enrollment documents, and ensure their institution head resubmits physical copies to the district office.

Students confused about which scheme to select on the portal, whether the state ADW scholarship or the GoI Post-Matric Scholarship, should know that both can often be applied for simultaneously since receiving one does not disqualify you from the other. Contact the scholarship helpline at 1800 599 7638 on Monday to Friday between 10 AM and 6 PM, or visit the district ADW office, for guidance on which scheme applies to your specific course and institution type.

extra_sections.text: The Adi Dravidar Welfare Department is one of Tamil Nadu's most wide-ranging educational support structures, covering everything from Rs 500 annual grants for primary school girls to Rs 50,000 startup assistance for law graduates. Every benefit flows directly to the bank account, with no cash and no middleman.

extra_sections.heading: Status Check and Escalation
content: If your portal status has shown pending for more than eight weeks after your institution confirmed dispatching the physical documents, visit your district ADW office in person with your application number and a copy of the submitted form. Long-pending applications are typically stuck at the district verification stage, and a direct visit with documentation resolves them significantly faster than repeated helpline calls or portal follow-ups.

faqs.question: What is the Adi Dravidar Welfare Department in Tamil Nadu?
faqs.answer:
The Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department is a Tamil Nadu state government department that runs educational scholarships, government hostels, and welfare schemes for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe communities, as well as Minority Muslims and Converted Christians. It administers scholarships from Class 1 through postgraduate level, operates its own school and hostel network, and provides targeted financial support to keep students from marginalised communities enrolled in education.

The official website is tnadw.tn.gov.in, and scholarship applications are submitted at ssp.tn.gov.in.

faqs.question: What is the income limit for Adi Dravidar Welfare scholarships?
faqs.answer:
For most ADW scholarships, including the Government of India Post-Matric Scholarship for SC students, the family income limit is Rs 2,50,000 per year. For Class 11 and Class 12 scholarships, the limit is stricter at Rs 1,00,000 per year.

Income must be certified by a Tehsildar or Revenue Divisional Officer, and the combined income of both parents is counted together. Certificates from panchayat presidents or self-declarations are not accepted, and the certificate must be from the current financial year.

faqs.question: How do I apply for the SC Adi Dravidar scholarship in Tamil Nadu?
faqs.answer:
Apply through the Tamil Nadu State Scholarship Portal at ssp.tn.gov.in by registering with your Aadhaar number, selecting the relevant scholarship scheme, and uploading your community certificate, income certificate, marksheets, and bank account details. After submitting the online form, your school or college head must also compile physical copies of all documents and send them to the district Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare office.

Both the online submission and the physical hard copy dispatch by the institution are mandatory steps, and the application will not be processed if either is missing.

faqs.question: What scholarships does the ADW department offer for college students?
faqs.answer:
For undergraduate and polytechnic students, the state ADW scholarship provides Rs 7,500 per year for academic expenses, and for PG and professional courses it provides Rs 8,000 per year. SC students can also simultaneously apply for the Government of India Post-Matric Scholarship, which covers all compulsory fees plus a monthly maintenance allowance of Rs 230 to Rs 550 for day scholars and Rs 380 to Rs 1,200 for hostellers depending on course level.

SC and ST law graduates starting their own practice after completing their degree can additionally receive a one-time startup grant of Rs 50,000.

faqs.question: Are government hostels available under Adi Dravidar Welfare?
faqs.answer:
Yes, the ADW department runs government hostels for SC and ST school students, college students, and ITI trainees across Tamil Nadu. Male students must live more than 5 kilometres from their institution to be eligible for a hostel seat, but girl students have no distance restriction and may apply regardless of proximity.

Hostel seats are allocated through the district ADW office and are limited, so students should apply early in the academic year for the best chance of being accommodated.

faqs.question: How do I check my Adi Dravidar Welfare scholarship application status?
faqs.answer:
Log in to ssp.tn.gov.in with your registered Aadhaar or mobile number and navigate to the application status section, which shows your application's progress at each stage from submission through district verification to directorate sanction. If your status has been pending for more than eight weeks after your institution dispatched the physical documents, visit the district ADW office directly with your application number for faster resolution.

You can also call the scholarship helpline at 1800 599 7638, available Monday to Friday from 10 AM to 6 PM.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for Adi Dravidar Welfare benefits in Tamil Nadu?
faqs.answer:
Students from Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Minority Muslim, and Converted Christian communities who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu for more than five years and whose annual family income does not exceed Rs 2,50,000 are eligible for most ADW scholarships. For Class 11-12 scholarships, the income limit is Rs 1,00,000.

Students must be enrolled in recognised schools or colleges in Tamil Nadu, and children of parents in occupations classified as unclean such as sanitation work are eligible regardless of the standard income limit.

faqs.question: What are the Chief Minister's Awards and special incentives under ADW?
faqs.answer:
The Chief Minister's Award is given to the 1,000 highest-scoring SC and ST boys and 1,000 highest-scoring SC and ST girls in the Tamil Nadu HSC Board exams each year, with each awardee receiving Rs 3,000 per year for five years to encourage them to pursue higher education. Additionally, the top 10 SC and ST students per district in the Class 10 Board exam get arranged admission to distinguished private schools for Class 11 and 12.

Free bicycles are provided to Class 11-12 SC Converted Christians under a related scheme, and all these incentives are administered through district ADW offices.
